words.ex: The young chess champion from Samarkand was invited onto a late-night talk show, where the host asked her about her childhood.
My little sister watches cartoons every Saturday morning; her favourite is about a family of talking bears.
The contestants on the game show had to answer ten questions correctly to win a new car.
Mum has been watching the same soap opera every weekday evening for twelve years; she worries about its characters as if they were our neighbours.
Last night we watched a documentary about how penguins keep their eggs warm through the long Antarctic winter.
The actors in this sitcom about three clumsy waiters at a hotel in Khiva are so funny that Dad spilled his tea laughing.
On the current affairs programme last night, two economists argued about whether bread prices will keep rising.
The presenter introduced each singer and told a short joke between the songs.
I can't wait for the next episode; the last one ended just as the detective found the missing key.
The weather forecast promised sunshine, so we left our umbrellas at home and got soaked on the way to the bazaar.
Within a day, the story of the boy who saved a puppy from the canal had spread through the mass media, from TV news to every website.
The film was in Turkish, but the Uzbek subtitles at the bottom of the screen helped us follow the story.
When I was little, the foreign films on TV were dubbed into Uzbek, so I never had to read anything.
Strong winds blew the satellite dish off our balcony, and we couldn't watch any channels for a week.
The film was interrupted by commercials every fifteen minutes, so it took three hours to finish.
I missed the final last night, but I can watch it on catch-up TV this evening.
The tabloid filled its front page with a photo of a footballer's new haircut and left almost no room for real news.
Our economics teacher reads a quality newspaper every morning for its long, careful articles on business and science.
Some websites care more about sensation than truth, so they make every small story sound shocking.
The football club was hit by a scandal when it turned out that two players had been paid to lose a match.
After years of writing for the school newspaper, Feruza decided to study journalism at university.
The magazine published an in-depth report on water shortages, with interviews, maps and statistics.
You need a subscription to read more than three articles a month on that news website.
Our school radio broadcasts music and short news reports every break, so you can hear it in all the corridors.
Our school's spring concert was televised on the local channel, and half the neighbourhood saw me forget my lines.
The adventure film was shot on location in the old streets of Khiva rather than in a studio.
The singer was tweeting photos from backstage while the audience were still looking for their seats.
Our class watched a historical drama about the court of Amir Temur, with actors in beautiful costumes.
For families living far apart, video calls are now the main means of communication.
With TV on demand, you can start any programme from the online library whenever you like.
This week's programme focuses on young farmers who grow vegetables without chemicals.
The director plans to shoot most of the film in the desert next spring.
As the host of the late-night show, Erkin chats with three famous guests every Friday.
I checked the TV listings in the paper to see what time the football started.
The seaside hotel offers newly-weds a free cake and a room with a balcony.
The magazine is full of photos of celebrities on the red carpet at film premieres.
